name: Foundation for Intentional Community (FIC)
description: A US-based 501(c)(3), incorporated in 1986, that serves the intentional communities movement — ecovillages, cohousing, and other shared-living communities — as a resource hub, publisher, network builder, and fiscal sponsor. It runs the ic.org directory where communities worldwide list themselves (self-submitted listings, which this site doesn't mirror), a Needs & Offers board for openings and housing, the Communities bookstore, podcasts, and CommUniversity: online courses, webinars, and virtual tours of real communities, many free or pay-what-you-can. Its stated mission is social, ecological, and economic justice and resiliency through cooperative culture and intentional communities. Its team works remotely around the world, and in 2026 it launched a shared website and directory with the Global Ecovillage Network.

notRepresentable: ic.org has a Groups section (https://www.ic.org/groups/), but it shows only a login screen to a logged-out visitor, so whether any group is active enough to clear the Forum bar couldn't be checked. Worth a look by someone with a free account.
research.notes: Events come from each CommUniversity page, not the /events collection, which is empty ("No Community in this collection") — the self-contradiction RESEARCH_QUEUE.md warned about. CommUniversity pages list times in US Central (the site's timezone is America/Chicago). Added: the Affordable Housing panel, the Equity & Power Dynamics course, Community Seeking 101, and the Oak Park Commons virtual tour. Left out: "Welcome Home" (2026-11-12), a launch party for the new FIC/GEN directory aimed at communities updating their listings; and the self-paced library courses (Finding Your Community, Starting a Community), which have no date. The Virtual Tour series is ongoing but publishes no cadence, so only the dated tour is listed; past tours are on FIC's YouTube channel. Needs & Offers is a classifieds board, not a discussion space, and each course's discussion group is only for enrolled students.
